title: Rust: gateway resource capability publication
description:
Connect actual gateway radio resources in rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs and rust/lichen-hal/src/lib.rs to publication in rust/lichen-gateway/src/capability_announcements.rs. Reuse the core finite-resource model to report supported channel/profile settings, simultaneous RX chains, TX chains, half-duplex exclusions, passband placement and demodulator limits under the finalized authenticated contract. Unknown or unsupported capability must not be represented as an available resource.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: This extracts capability publication from the former rust.14 scope. rust.05 owns the core resource model, rust.02 the wire boundary, rust.09 shared report semantics and rust.13 the integrated node path; do not duplicate those mechanisms or create new hardware support. rust.14.admission separately owns gateway traffic wiring. Preserve radio-owned identity, upstream Yggdrasil, baseline SCHC/security and best-effort custody; portability is deferred and audited OSCORE/EDHOC remains untouched. No hardware access, RF activation or measured-capability claim is authorized.
acceptance_criteria: Consume independent vectors.02/.04 through production capability extraction and publication, checking frozen bytes and explicit resource tables. Test one radio, multiple RX/one TX, disjoint/restricted passbands, finite demodulators, unsupported profiles and missing capability data. Assert tunable channel count, scanning and a concentrator type name cannot manufacture parallel reception. Extend rust/lichen-gateway/tests and focused HAL capability tests with deterministic backends. Run hosted tests using current manifests, affected shared-crate --no-default-features checks, fmt and scoped clippy; do not use production publication as its own oracle.
